description:
From: JSON. Filed with user approval ("proceed" on /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-mue.25.html, section 5, 2026-11-24). Reviewed by fz-engine.

Today: a loop entered at k functions is copied once per entry point. The json decoder loop (36 functions entered at 12) yields about 431 function instances; 12 copies fall into at most 4 classes by settled results. Copies spend 4,128 of 9,858 analysis runs (42%).

Mechanism: when a loop's work group closes (crates/fz-engine/src/groups.rs; scheduler.rs:836, :1004-1048), copies whose settled results are equivalent are merged. Rules:
- The merge is recomputed at every close from that close's settled results; a close means settled until the group reopens.
- Downstream reads only the merged result, never a copy, so a reopen that splits copies again wakes their readers.
- A merge that later splits is a withdrawal; this rests on fz-t93.27's withdrawal rule and adds none of its own.
- Equivalence is type equivalence per column, as the store already compares rows, not equal Ty handles.

Saves emission and downstream work (json: 12 copies to at most 4); not the copies' analysis.

Gate: build only after fz-t93.7.2 is measured (the remaining saving may be small), and re-count group reopens after fz-t93.27 (json reopened 27 times, 24 from the root-wide Raisable fact).

Evidence: JSON's scratch mue25/probes p1, p3, p4; summary /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/mue25/fable_review.md.
title: Loop copies whose settled results are identical are emitted once
